Anne Arundel County, Maryland Tax Lien Sales: A Great Investment Opportunity

Imagine locking in up to an 18% annual return on your investment! You can do just that with Anne Arundel County, Maryland’s annual Tax Lien Sale. This online event provides a straightforward way to invest in property while helping the county recover overdue taxes. Here’s how you can get started and what you need to know.

Important Details for Tax Lien Investors

Anne Arundel County’s tax lien certificate sales are held once a year, typically in May or June. The bidding process happens entirely online, making it easy and accessible for investors from anywhere.

How the Auction Works

  • Bidding Format: Public auction, where the highest bidder wins.
  • Bidder Registration: Required online, with a W-9 form and a $100 registration fee.
  • Payments: Payments must be made by wire transfer or cashier’s check by 3 PM the following day.
  • Interest Rate: The interest rate on successful bids is 18% annually (1.5% per month).

If you’re successful in purchasing a tax lien certificate, the property owner has two years to redeem the property by paying the amount due (including interest and any accrued taxes). If they don’t redeem, you can initiate foreclosure procedures.

Foreclosure Process and Risks

  • Redemption Period: The owner has up to two years to redeem the property. If they don’t redeem, you can start the foreclosure process through the Anne Arundel County Circuit Court.
  • Certificate of Sale: After six months, a certificate of sale is issued. This document gives you the right to start the foreclosure process if the property owner has not redeemed the lien.
  • Risks: As with any investment, risks are involved. Anne Arundel County sells properties as-is, and the county does not guarantee the marketability of the title.

Steps to Participate

Research and Understand Local Laws:

Knowing the legal framework is crucial. The Maryland Annotated Code, Tax-Property Article § 14-812, outlines key regulations.

Visit the Local Treasurer’s Website:

Check out the Anne Arundel County Finance Department for specific details on the tax sale.

Register for the Auction:

Complete the registration form, including a W-9 and the $100 registration fee.

Submit Your Bids:

Submit bids in Excel format. Mind the high bid premium for bids over 40% of the property’s assessed value.

Make Your Payment:

Payments must be made via cash or certified check.

Understand Redemption and Foreclosure:

The redemption period is nine months for owner-occupied residential properties and six months for other properties. After this period, you may initiate foreclosure if the property owner hasn’t paid the owed taxes.

Fun Facts About Anne Arundel County

Key Details for Anne Arundel County Tax Lien Sales

Population: As of 2020, the population is 588,261, which is an increase of nearly 10% since 2010.

County Seat: Annapolis, which is also the state capital of Maryland.

History: The county honors Anne Arundell, a member of a prominent English family.

Economic Hub: Anne Arundel County belongs to the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson metro area, which is also part of the Washington-Baltimore-Arlington combined metro area.

Pro Tips

  • Due Diligence: Research the properties thoroughly before bidding. Remember, the county sells properties as-is.
  • Follow-up: If you don’t win your desired properties, unsold liens may be available about a week later.
  • Keep Records: Maintain detailed records of your bids and payments for tax reporting purposes.
